title: I Am No Longer Your Negro

sense.text:
“Stay yourselves, and wonder” is a message to us, the enlightened ones, the Israelite prophets. Stay yourselves means stay in the Bible, stabilize yourself in it. We woke up, and then we look out and see our people in abject mental destruction, destroyed mentally, and we are kept stable by the wisdom and knowledge in this book and the commandments.

We wonder when we see our people with that psychotic behavior, that chaotic behavior, acting like court jesters, like quote unquote super predators, a wolf pack, a menace to society. How did my people get like this? How did this happen? And how could we administer the medicine to cure his sickness and her sickness? That is the wondering. We are performing surgery on this creation called the negro. All surgery hurts, but at the end of it you are going to be all right: it surgically removes that madness from our people’s minds, to release them from the chains of being a negro in spirit, in all the tribes. We are no longer Esau’s experiment. We are no longer his negro.

“Cry ye out, and cry”: once we see the despair, the hopelessness, the degradation, the mental depletion, no real manhood, we go back to this wisdom and knowledge and apply the medicine by crying out to fix them, letting our people know they are in lies and in denial.

“They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink.” Getting high and drunkenness fall under hard liquor and under hard drugs: crack, cocaine, marijuana, fentanyl. They are designed to kill you, but before they kill you they put you in a euphoric state and suspend you from reality. When a person drinks, he staggers; when he puts the needle in his arm or smokes crack, he staggers; that is why there are laws against getting behind the wheel. But this verse excludes those, to show what kind of high it is speaking of. Our people stagger, but not because of alcohol and not because they are smoking crack. They are staggering in lies. They are staggering in Christianity.

Alcohol is on one level, the crack and heroin are another level of suspending yourself from reality, and the church is equated with them: it has the same effect, perhaps worse. Alcohol, hard drugs and Christianity are all designed to remove you from the reality of what you really see. That is escapism: the tendency to seek distraction and relief from unpleasant realities, especially by seeking entertainment or engaging in fantasy, the fantasy of the Christian church and the fallacy of a white Jesus. You seek distraction in a bottle, in a needle, in church, and you deny the potency of it: the functional crack addict, the alcoholic who says I can handle this. Church is the same thing. People go into the crack house, I mean the church, smoke that white Jesus, and come out black just like you. The people in the churches are just as drugged up as the man on the corner with crack, and just as drunk as the people on alcohol.

The unpleasant realities are the conditioning, the drunkenness of the negro mentality that we all have. Negro is not a skin color; even thinking that it is, is a white supremacist thing. It is a mental condition: they conditioned us to be a certain way, so that we think negro and think a black person, and do not think of the native indigenous and the Latinos, all those that fit the curses.

Fantasy describes the negro mind one hundred percent today: all day in video games, all day wanting to be an NBA player, dreaming and daydreaming but never doing anything to bring forth what they think about, and running from realism. Anytime our people hear us bring them reality, all of a sudden they have to go. The American dream falls under it too: a pipe dream, romanticizing what it means to be a part of this country, the illusion of inclusion. Since they did away with DEI, you really see what they think about us, every time the President or anybody in his cabinet speaks. They try to deny it, but it is obvious as long as you are not caught up in this escapism.

Getting high suspends you above the reality of where you live, a temporary suspension; when you come down you are back inside the reality and your problems are still there. Terms like functional, put in front of alcoholic or crackhead, normalize it and soften the blow, but years later, months later, the insides are eaten up. That is denial of the facts.

The church goes along with the drugs because the realities of why the people are in there are never addressed. That is why a lot of men are not in there: men need reality. The preacher is using up the women, who are looking for Mr. Good, and the preacher has more power than all of the women’s husbands put together.

“For the Lord hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep”: the people in the churches are in a deep sleep. The Lord has poured it out upon those in the crack house, I mean the church; crack house and church are the same thing.

“And hath closed your eyes”: they have closed their eyes to their reality because they are still high. They cannot even see themselves in the Bible they are reading. The same book they are supposed to be learning from literally has their condition in it, and they cannot see it. That is serious blindness. One of those 2819 churches has the people sitting in the dark; they cannot even see the Bible. You cannot get more mockery than that.

“The prophets and your rulers”: the man up there giving out the spiritual dope and the people listening to it are all blind. “The seers hath he covered”: the pastors cannot teach you anything because they themselves are high on the white man’s Christianity.

“And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed”: the vision of all the people in that crack house, that church, the preacher included, is sealed. The people come in with all kinds of problems, but the preacher is unable to show them their problems in the Bible, so it might as well be a sealed book. The Bible is not made tangible to their actual lives. They are in there finger popping, swinging, jumping up and down and dancing, but they are not getting the medicine the Bible has for them. All of that is the negro.

“Which men deliver to one that is learned”: the learned one is the big mega church preacher, who learned those Christian lies from the white man. One of the few in the church pulls a Bible out of his pocket and brings it to the pastor: Listen, preacher, I am in here cracked out, but I read something in Deuteronomy 28 about ships; show me what this means. “And he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed”: he asks, have you been washed in the blood of Jesus, and says all kinds of things, but never addresses what you brought him. It is like they say of the book of Revelation: God has not opened that up to anybody.

“The book is delivered to him that is not learned”: this is the overnight preacher, the hole in the wall, the storefront preacher. He has not been to school, no seminary, nothing; he has not received his doctrine from the council on religions, the top people. They tell him he has not been to their cemetery schools, I mean seminary schools, buried in a crooked theology.

“And he saith, I am not learned”: I have not gone to those schools; go to the T.D. Jakes ones, go to the dancing, cutting up ones, the 2819s; I am just a storefront. He still cannot give you the answer. None of them is giving you the truth.

“This people draw near me with their mouth”: they are in there jumping up and down like a bunch of wild hyenas, cutting up in those churches, going wild and crazy, howling. “And with their lips do honour me”: we love the blood of Jesus, the letters of Paul, Galatians, such and such. They throw all kinds of scriptures out like a tape recorder injected into them; you hear the words of the Bible, but they know nothing about what they just said. They say they honor Jesus and the Bible. That is still the effect of dope in negro Christianity.

“But have removed their heart far from me”: they will not keep one commandment. They do not want to hear anything about God’s high holy days, the dietary law, the ceremonial law, the civil laws, nothing, though Christ said out of his own mouth, if you love me, keep my commandments. They cannot even read that. That shows the effect of Christianity, which is crack, which is white supremacy: it is all the same thing, and it locks you out of reality.

“And their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men”: the white man taught them how to deliver the potency of Christianity, inject it into their brains and make them all negroes. All of them are drug dealers: one has the crack needle, one the rock, one the cocaine, one the hard liquor, and the other has Christianity in all its flavors to jack your minds up. And they are on the corner too: in New York you find four or five little churches on every block, with the drugs, the smoke shop and the liquor store beside them, and the whole block is destroyed. The white man taught them how to ingest that lie, and they stagger with it. Total denial. That is the negro.

The top ones know that the people coming into those lying churches are the Israelites. Their job is to keep them asleep, because the more of them that wake up, the more that number is sealed and they lose everything. So the oppressor, the crack dealer in the church, keeps the Israelites in docility in the scriptures. That is why there is such hatred against what we are doing, and it is a real fight to get rid of the negro mentality in the whole nation, all the tribes, blacks, Hispanics and Indians alike.

precepts.why:
“Stay yourselves” is answered here: “And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times, and strength of salvation.” The wisdom and knowledge is the Bible. That is what stabilizes us when we look upon unstable times and see our people operating in an unstable condition. We know where the stability is; they are not connected to it, and that is what causes us to wonder as we look upon them.

This wisdom and knowledge is also the strength of our salvation. Those of us who are enlightened know there is a salvation after this sickness that we see. Our brothers and sisters do not have that knowledge; they think wherever they are now is permanent, and they are completely lost. Once we are enlightened, we are not going back to our old vomit.

“The fear of the Lord is his treasure.” We have fear of the Lord by staying in this Bible and meditating on it, because we know what is written in it is real. Staying in this written word, we can vividly see our people standing on the verses. When you read Deuteronomy 28, the cargo slave ships are sitting on 28:68 and the yokes of iron are sitting on 28:48; the imagery comes up in your mind as you read. That is the power of the words: they interact with your spirit, and the spirit bears witness that we are the Israelites, the children of the living Father. We stand on that knowledge.

“Cry ye out” goes with this: “Cry aloud, spare not, lift up thy voice like a trumpet, and shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins.” Our people do not want the medicine. Crying out is us being the doctors who say you have to take the medicine anyway: you refuse the doctor’s orders, but you are a patient about to die, so we have to give it to you anyway, and give it loud, like a trumpet, to make sure you hear it in an effort to save your life.

Transgressions and sins are what is going to kill our people, for the wages of sin is death. So as we bring this out, we are trying to save their lives, though they resist the medicine. That is our job: to show the Israelites, the house of Jacob, their sins.

There are limits: cast not your pearls among swine. Some of us heard this gospel several times before we made the step; some walked past the camp for years. The Lord sends the spirit to listen when it is that one’s time to wake up. You do not jump down and try to make him; you cry aloud as the scripture says, keep teaching, and the Most High deals with the rest. If he means for that spirit to get right, he will come back, hear one scripture and say you do not have to tell me any more, I am in.

This is escapism in the Bible. We come to our people with the real gospel, and it is supposed to be healing, but because they are so caught up in smoking white Jesus, they would rather live the lie, the pipe dream. “That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the Lord”: we know we are lying outwardly, but we are lying to ourselves as well when we accept the Christianity, the Catholicism, the alcohol and all the other means of escapism that keep us in that negro state of mind.

“Which say to the seers, See not; and to the prophets, Prophesy not unto us right things”: don’t tell me how not to be a negro anymore. That is when they go to the apologists for the verse of the week, the one they send around in a memo to trip us up. They do not study the scriptures; any of our people who went back and truly studied what we brought out, even to gainsay it, would be converted if they were Israelites and it was the Lord’s will. “Speak unto us smooth things, prophesy deceits.” That is escapism.

“Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us”: they do not want to deal with it. Don’t give me the real Christ, don’t give me reality; give me the pipe dream, the fairy tale.

So when they go to their apologetic high priests, they only go to find ways to stay asleep: give me the stronger dope, so when I pass by the camp I can leave with my crack habit and my lies intact. They know they are in a mess. Who goes to a hospital who does not need a cure? Why would they be going into a church if they did not need help? Yet they come out and pass by the real physicians with the leg still messed up and the head still messed up; the countenance is still the same and witnesses against them. They go all the way around the camp to avoid it, and the girls coming out in a string for a dress start pulling it down when they come near, because they feel convicted. That tells you nobody is teaching them anything; if the pastor were telling them what he should, they would not feel that way at all.

sense.text:
Where there is no vision, we become prisoners of false hope. Our people have been made to be men ready to die, and die for foolishness, with no vision and no hope to live. When real hope is deferred because it is out of your reach, you become mentally sick, and that is the ghetto mentality.

The Lord did not waste his time creating you to be nothing. There were decisions made in the heavens to have you born at that time, rather than hundreds, thousands, perhaps millions of other spirits; something in us knows we have a greater purpose. Men have a conscience that questions their reality: why is my life going like this, what purpose do I have, what should I do? When you cannot find the answers to that voice that tells you how you should be as a man, how you should be as a woman, “Hope deferred maketh the heart sick.” It makes the mind sick, plagued with what I should do and unable to find the method to get it done. A frustration builds up in your psychology and your spirit, a battle goes on in you, and you end up going crazy, outside the drugs, outside the alcohol and even outside the church, and you end up in a psych unit.

Instead of being men and dealing with that voice, we drown it out with alcohol, with drugs, and even by going to church. The educational system did not give us the tools, the churches did not give them to us, and nobody took the time to teach us how to properly live, so every time the question comes up we feel inept to answer it.

“But when the desire cometh, it is a tree of life.” When you finally get that clean glass of water, it is a tree of life. That is what happened to the Bishop: he wondered why his people suffered the way they did, why Harlem had the crack and all the foolishness and evil, and that drove him looking through different philosophies. To a thirsty man anything wet will do, but Kool-Aid is wet and will not quench your thirst; something is still missing. He drank Africanism and Islam, and the thirst was still there. Some were impressive, but they did not tell him who he was. When he came to the truth, all the answers came in, and thirty-four years later he has not looked any further: his thirst has been quenched. Everybody still in those other things keeps asking questions because their thirst has not been properly quenched, and that is why they will not stop and talk when we are out there teaching. The Bible, the commandments, show us who we are and why these things happened to us.

This is catharsis in the Bible: purgative, purging, cleansing. “But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth.” In that great house, some vessels will burn and some are pure and cannot burn. The house will burn down if you have tinder in it, the wood and the earth.

The house is the man. “If a man therefore purge himself from these”: that is catharsis. The wood and the earth are the things you are holding in. You see it on a grand scale in us as a people, and you see it in brothers and sisters individually who have bitterness in their hearts; those things eat you up inside and burn you up.

“He shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified”, which means cleansed, “and meet for the master’s use”: then you are ready to serve the Lord, and you cannot be while you hold those things in. “And prepared unto every good work.” That is part of the transforming process that repentance does for you when you purge it out of you. We have to be able to tell our story and get those things off our chest.

A cathartic feeling is one of purification after expressing strong or repressed emotions, leading to a sense of relief and mental balance. The black and Hispanic communities, our children, our men and our women, are the way they are because we have not been able to express what we have seen with our own eyes for centuries, and we are ridiculed by this white nation for it, which leads to an imbalanced mental state. The only thing that can cure that is the Bible. Talking about it on talk shows and in intellectual circles means nothing; the power is in knowing that God acknowledges what happened to you. When you read in the greatest book on the planet that he knows what happened to you, that he loves you and is going to punish those that did it, the dots connect, your mental balance is restored, and that is the cathartic relief we needed. That is the clean water.

This addresses what the vacuum of leadership caused. When Malcolm X was killed in 1965 and Dr. Martin Luther King in 1968, our leaders were killed off and a vacuum of father figures was created, just as James Baldwin lost his mentor when his friend jumped. From that point rage built up; we were living in despair and confusion, and here came the drugs, the dope, the heroin, and then the jails. That was a systematic killing of our people, and that is what the black man’s face is hiding.

“Turn you to the strong hold, ye prisoners of hope”: that is us, the Israelites. We live in a society that has robbed our hope from us, and we are prisoners of hope, looking for a nation that cannot save us. Having no real hope, we turned to cocaine and heroin; people overdosed and lay dead in the alleys of Harlem with the needle still in their arm. “Even to day do I declare that I will render double unto thee.”

“When I have bent Judah for me”: listen to what the Most High is getting ready to do. He is going to build us up and put us in order. He makes Judah as a bow; that is what bent means. “Filled the bow with Ephraim”: Ephraim is the arrow. The Lord is creating a bow and arrow, a weapon.

“And raised up thy sons, O Zion”, all twelve tribes, “against thy sons, O Greece.” O Greece lets you know who Esau is: the white man. “And made thee as the sword of a mighty man”: the Most High is going to make us as the sword of a mighty man.

But before we get to that physical battle axe, we have to get rid of the negro mind and the undisciplined spirit. We have to get our minds right first. The Lord said wait upon me, because he is the one who is going to make it happen. The only thing he needs from us is to be disciplined in keeping his laws and getting our minds right in this truth.

“And the Lord shall be seen over them.” This was read to tell the brothers who want to go do something extra: no. When this goes down, the Lord is going to be over us to make sure it happens. Some brothers want to run with something, and they are not even disciplined. We are not a hate group and do not advocate violence against anyone; a brother who goes to start something now will get slaughtered. Get your mind right first, so that the Most High will find you fit, and when he gets behind it he will make the change that needs to go down.

Right now we need to be learning this Bible and getting ourselves together: stop the stupidness, the alcohol and the craziness in the body, and get our discipline together. If we cannot even get that together, forget about all of this; you will get rolled over by it.

precepts.why:
Judah as the bow and Ephraim as the arrow is what this speaks of: “Thou art my battle axe and weapons of war.” The Most High says that we, the nation of Israel, are his battle axe and weapons of war.

“For with thee will I break in pieces the nations, and with thee will I destroy kingdoms”: the Most High is going to use us Israelites as a threshing instrument. “And with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider; and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and his rider; With thee also will I break in pieces man and woman; and with thee will I break in pieces old and young; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the maid.” It is going to be a hell of a time when the Most High builds us up.

That is where we are going to get to, but we have to get our minds right first. Brothers are not to do some craziness and try to start something now. The Most High is stirring many things up in the earth right now for the controversy of Zion, as Deacon Malachi brought out in his last class, but we have to get ourselves right first and be able to tell our story.

“Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them”: that is what we have been looking at all class long, the evil of what they have done to us.

“Therefore thus saith the Lord God; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom”: the Most High says he is going to stretch his hand upon our enemies. “And will cut off man and beast from it”: that is the horse and the rider read in Jeremiah 51. “And I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword”: he is going to cut off their wise as well as their dumb ones, their whole nation.

“And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel.” God said he will do it, so God is going to do it. That is the battle axe and weapons of war the Most High is going to make out of the same people who are regarded as nothing. This is the same thing as raising up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece: the Most High is the one who will set it all up and change all of that.

sense.text:
This is the rage seen in the Bronx: the brother who broke heads to feel relief, and the boy the gang dragged out of the bodega in 2018 and hacked up with machetes, a boy who had nothing to do with it. That is the negro, in Northern Kingdom too.

“Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”: all that frustration, no catharsis, all the things they cannot speak about, all of it a product of the negro mindset built up inside: rage, anger, frustration, and no answers anywhere for them. We know the answer is in this Bible; that is the only medicine that is going to heal them.

“They are full of the fury of the Lord”: it goes back to the frustration, like the brother saying, give us a chance. “The rebuke of thy God”: why is it the rebuke of God? Because we are in these conditions for what we did and what we continue not to acknowledge. The Lord gave us daylight and a way out, but instead of taking the right medicine, we take the other options: we break heads, we join gangs to feel seen. They created that mindset and that environment, and then the apologists use the same language about us that they use for gangs, as if offering identity in righteousness were a bad thing.

We give our people the light to not be this way and to not have that fury: not for us to take our hands and do violence, but to use God’s words to burn up all those lies, take that same fire, passion and frustration and channel it into righteousness. The Lord has pulled us out of a dark place; now we lift up our next brother and our next sister and enlighten each one of them.

On the reservation, the Gadites are drowning in the same thing: the brother who hopes the tidal wave comes back and brings some more beer is saying, let me get high so I can disconnect from this ugly reality; let me waste myself in this bottle. All the tribes face the same negro mind. God did not put him here to do that, and the Most High did not cause us to be born to end up like this.

The Lord said that before he formed you in the belly he knew you. That means our spirits existed with the Lord before he put your spirit into that sperm and egg to cause you to be born into this earth. Decisions were made in the heavens: I want you here rather than him, rather than her, at this time. There is a reason for that decision, which means you have a purpose.

Then we get here and our lives are wasted, to the point where the brother asked whether it matters if he lives or dies had to think about it. Is my life even worth living? You damn right it is: God made it and saw fit to have you born. But if you are disconnected from where you really belong, you will not see that; you will devalue yourself everywhere you go and let anything run over you, as if you are not even worth being heard. That is why our stories have to be told, turned all the way up, so our people can resonate with them. It is cathartic.
